the Highway Authority objects to the planning application
The application site is located within a rural and inherently unsustainable location
Kington Lane is characterised as a narrow, single-lane rural route with limited opportunity for passing and no associated footway, street lighting or parking restrictions in the vicinity.

The site is not located within reasonable walking distance of day-to-day services, facilities or public transport infrastructure. The nearest bus stops and bus services are located approximately 1km from the site, whilst Claverdon Railway Station is approximately 2.5km away. Access to these facilities would require pedestrians to travel along rural roads without the benefit of footways or street lighting.

There are no dedicated footways linking the site to local facilities, public transport or services. As a result, pedestrians would be required to walk within the carriageway of Kington Lane, which is unlit and rural in character.
This is particularly relevant for vulnerable users, including children, older persons and those travelling during periods of darkness or adverse weather conditions.

The footway along Henley road is very narrow at points, for example alongside Bankside Cottage where the speed limit remains 50mph, and does not provide an accessible route into the village. It is well below the 2m standard width and too narrow for a pushchair/buggy to be easily accommodated.

This application is not sustainable from an active travel perspective. There are no suitable and accessible pedestrian routes into Claverdon which will lead to a reliance on motor vehicles for short journeys.
However, this land has not been identified within either the red-line application boundary or the blue-line ownership plan.
